confidence_explanation: The timeline shows a clear progression from automated SQL injection attempts to a successful account takeover, privilege escalation, massive database querying, and subsequent data exfiltration via DNS tunneling and HTTPS, followed by an attempt to cover tracks by deleting logs.

attack_chain.description: Automated SQL injection attempts using sqlmap targeting the /api/items endpoint from IP 162.247.74.27.
Successful login of user_01 from the same suspicious IP (162.247.74.27) used in the SQL injection attempts, occurring during off-hours.
Unauthorized privilege escalation where user_01 elevated their role to 'dba'.
Massive database queries executed by user_01 against the 'prod_main' database, retrieving hundreds of thousands of rows from the 'customers' table.
Data exfiltration begins via DNS tunneling (UDP port 53) to a known malicious domain 'x8327.malicious-83.com'.
Large volume of data exfiltration via HTTPS (TCP port 443) to an external destination.
Attempt to cover tracks by deleting the authentication log (/var/log/auth.log).

gaps: Confirmation of whether the SQL injection (evt_s91_001) was the direct mechanism used to obtain user_01's credentials.
Identification of the destination IP for the HTTPS exfiltration.
narrative: An attacker used SQL injection to likely compromise user_01's credentials, then logged in from a suspicious IP to escalate privileges to DBA. After querying massive amounts of customer data, the attacker exfiltrated the data via DNS and HTTPS before attempting to delete system logs to hide the intrusion.
